explanation: Record the stream values in a hash set, then scan nonnegative integers from zero. The first absent candidate satisfies the contract; negative stream values do not affect the scan.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected Set scanning checks at most n+1 candidates; bucket variants perform two full passes and fixed-size scans.
spaceComplexity: O(n) Set entries, bucket arrays and Python tee buffering are explicitly accounted for above.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: The set contains every input value. Scanning from zero stops only at an absent nonnegative integer, so the returned value satisfies the required range and absence condition. With n supplied values, some candidate among 0 through n must be absent.
walkthrough: For [0,1,3], candidates 0 and 1 are present and 2 is absent. Return 2; the structural adapter independently verifies that it is nonnegative and not in the input.
edgeCases: Repeated input values do not block additional candidates.
An empty stream can return zero.
Negative values do not change which nonnegative candidates are absent.
